content.content:
the error and mark the reference failed; none reads the text.

A 404 whose body says the proxy's upstream is blocked is marked (DEVDESK-632):
`registryStatusError(resp)` (`internal/oci/status_body.go`) builds the
`*StatusError` of every non-200 registry answer (tags, catalog, `ManifestDigest`)
and, for a 404 only, reads at most 4 KiB of the body (`maxStatusBody`, a
hypothesis like `maxNexusErrorBody`). When the body is JSON and the `message` of
the first `errors[]` entry starts with `Remote Auto Blocked` (exact, case
sensitive, no leading space), `UpstreamBlocked()` is true. A missing, empty,
plain-text, longer or cut body, another message, another status (502,
  in a registry URL (`https://alice:...@host`) reaches neither the footer nor
  `log.Printf`.
- **The Nexus detector** (`internal/registrymgr/nexus.go`) has the same origin
  guard (`nexusHTTPClient.CheckRedirect = oci.RefuseOffOriginRedirect`, 8 s
  timeout unchanged) and reads each reply through
  `oci.ReadAllLimited(..., maxNexusResponse)`, 1 MiB. The cap is a hypothesis,
  not measured. The anonymous retry of the group members still happens on any
  error but a refused off-origin redirect (see `registries.md`); the first
  attempt decides the outcome, the retry only changes it by succeeding.
  `fetchGroupMembers` no longer swallows its errors (DEVDESK-510): a
  `StatusError` from the management API with 401 or 403, or the 404 Nexus
  answers a pull account (DEVDESK-578), becomes
  `*registrymgr.MembersRefusedError` (`errors.Is(err, ErrMembersRefused)`,
  `Group`, `Status`, `Anonymous`; its text holds the group and the status,
  never a URL or a body; for the 404, `Cause` is the plain
  `*oci.StatusError`), any other error is returned as it is. `nexusGET` reads
  the body of a 404 only, up to 4 KiB (`maxNexusErrorBody`, a hypothesis: the
  measured body is about 50 bytes), and only to check that its JSON `message`
  is `Repository not found`; the body never reaches an error or a log. A 404
  with any other body, or a longer one, stays a plain status error. A reply
  without a `group.memberNames` key (empty body, `null`, `{}`) is an error;
and `AddImageResults` takes it (false when stale; `pendingSearches` never goes
under 0).

**Verdicts per registry (DEVDESK-303, IS-12).** `AddImageResults` calls
`imagesearch.Classify` in `Update`, never in the `Cmd` (Rule 110), and stores the
result in `RegistryBrowser.outcomes`, keyed by `EntryKey`. The map is reset by
`startImageSearch`, so it holds one lot only; a registry with no entry is still
pending. Only an `ok` verdict appends rows. `Outcome(entryKey)` reads one
verdict (false while pending). `Model.RegistryBrowserOutcomes()` returns a copy
of the map, or nil when the browser is closed; it is for the tests and for IS-13.

The Nexus verdicts below rest on measures made on the local bench, not on a
company instance: read "Measured Nexus behavior" after this section before
trusting a verdict for another Nexus.

**Image search and Nexus members (DEVDESK-579, NX-12).** `targetFor` sets
`CatalogUnderPrefix` on two kinds of entry: a plain entry that lists cached
content only and has a `repo_prefix` (a `parent:` entry of a `provider: nexus`
group), and a discovered member of a Nexus group that has a `repo_prefix`. The two
tests are equivalent, because `checkRepoPrefixes` refuses a `repo_prefix` on a
group. Any other entry keeps the root catalog and guard R1.

`searchUnits` decides what a lot searches. Discovered members **without an
address of their own** (same URL and same `repo_prefix` as their group, with the
group's slug as `ParentSlug`) are merged into **one** unit, the group, labelled
`<alias> (group)` (`groupUnitSuffix`). It is walked once, and its rows name no
member: Nexus does not say which member holds a name. By design this bypasses the
picker's selection: ticking one bare member searches the whole group, and a row can
carry the name of a member that was unticked. A group that was not discovered (a
pull account) is searched as itself, with its bare label. The Registry column
keeps the whole suffix when it cuts a cell (`datatable.Column.KeepSuffix`, see
`ui-components.md`). `lotUnits` holds the units of the current lot until the next
image search; `entryFor` falls back on it, so labels, the `→` tags drill of a group
row and the `r` filter work on a unit. The `?` help says: `'nx (group)': images
found through the group; Nexus does not say which member holds each one.`

**Level 1 header summary (DEVDESK-305, IS-13).** `searchHeaderInfo`
(`browser_summary.go`, called from `GetHeaderInfo`) says what the lot did, one
header line per class, in this order: `Images` (the row count, always), then
`Pending` (a count, live lot) or `Interrupted` (names, the lot was abandoned
with the left arrow before they answered), `Failed` (red), `Refused`, `Partial`
(orange), `May omit images` (orange, DEVDESK-308 IS-14, reworded by DEVDESK-629 F2), `No result` (dim) and `Skipped` (dim, catalog not walked because the
query is shorter than `imagesearch.CatalogMinQueryRunes`). A class with nothing
to say has no line, so a lot where every registry answered shows only `Images`.
`summarizeSearch` (pure) sorts the lot's keys into the classes. A name is the
Registry column's label (`entryLabel`: alias, else URL, else key), in form order.
`Partial` lists registries cut at a cap, `No result` those that answered with
nothing (Skipped excluded). A registry that is both partial and empty appears
on both lines, on purpose.

`May omit images` lists the registries that may not have listed every image
they hold, by their role in a Nexus group (DEVDESK-629, F2; it replaces the
`Cached only` line of DEVDESK-308, whose "limited to cached content" reading the
measures of NX-04 contradicted). `browserRegistryEntry.role` is a `nexusRole`
(group, proxy, hosted, unknown), set once by `buildEntries`: a
`provider: nexus` + `kind: group` entry is a group; a discovered member of one
takes `memberRole(RegistryGroupMember.Type)` (`hosted`, `proxy`, `group`; any
other value, case included, is unknown); a declared entry whose `parent` is the
slug of a Nexus group takes the type of the discovered member at its exact
`(URL, RepoPrefix)`, and is unknown when none matches or the cache predates the
type (H5); a group unit (`groupUnit`) is a group. `isNexusGroupOrMember` (the
former `listsCacheOnly`) only drives `catalogUnderPrefix`. The pure rule is
`mayOmit(role, outcome)`: a group whatever it answered (it says nothing about
what a member it could not reach left out), a proxy only when it `failed` or was
`refused`, a hosted repository never, an unknown role never (no mention is better
than a false one), and never a `Skipped` outcome. `summarizeSearch` takes a
`func(string) nexusRole` and reads it by entry key (`entryRole`, not by slug:
members share their group's slug). A group that answered with no result is
marked ` (no result)` on that line and is not on `No result`; the mark does not
mean the image is absent, only that this registry listed nothing and may have
left out what it could not reach, while `No result: quay` means the registry
answered and holds nothing that matches. A `failed` or `refused` mention stays on
its own line too and carries no mark; a partial registry appears on `Partial` and
on `May omit images`. Docker Hub, generic registries and a Nexus outside a group
never get the line. `Skipped` and `May omit images` exclude each other (`Skipped`
means no catalog entry answered), which keeps the budget below. The search sends
no request to the members of a group (F4): the group answers on its own connector,
and a member the group could not reach is invisible to DevDesk; the line says it
may happen, it cannot say it did. The MCP server is unchanged.
The Nexus catalog tests of `internal/imagesearch` (`TestCatalogOnMeasuredNexusAnswers`)
replay answers measured on the bench (Nexus 3.98.1-01, NX-03), not hand-written
ones: the verdicts `ok`, `No result` and `Refused` (prefix absent from a real
catalog) are checked there. `Failed` and the group line are measured since NX-04
(DEVDESK-580, PR3): a proxy's catalog lists names it does not hold
(`mirror/uncached`) while its upstream answers, and a group on its connector answers
`no result` for `mirror` once a member's upstream is cut, which is why `(no result)`
does not mean absent.
See "Recorded fixtures" in [`nexus-bench.md`](nexus-bench.md).

**Measured Nexus behavior (NX-03, NX-04, NX-05).** Where the code rests on how
Nexus answers, this is what was observed and what was not. Every row was
50:  `/v2/<repo_prefix>/_catalog`. Nexus answers with names that do not carry the
53:- **Any other entry** walks the root catalog of its host (`/v2/_catalog`), keeps

Upstream cut: the first `_catalog` read gets a 502 after about 20 s, then the proxy auto-blocks and answers 404 `Remote Auto Blocked until <date>` to `_catalog` and `tags/list`, even for an image in its cache; a HEAD still serves the cached image (200) and 404s the uncached one. # The nexus-bench:* tasks (DEVDESK-504, docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md) drive a
# disposable Nexus on a real k0s cluster through kubectl: up, provision, down,
# seed, cut-upstream, restore-upstream, reset and status read or change that
# cluster, and the bench has to be reachable from this machine. They are NOT
# part of ci, check, test or test-race and nothing depends on them
# (mise_tasks_test.go checks it). Only render contacts nothing, and record
# (DEVDESK-511) reaches the bench through its loopback ports, not the cluster.
#
# kubectl is declared on each task that reaches the cluster rather than in
# [tools], so the CI does not install it; render and record reach no cluster and
# have none.
# seed (DEVDESK-505) also needs skopeo, which is a tool of the host: mise does
# not install it and the description of the task says so.
# The cluster (datomir) runs k0s v1.36.x and kubectl is supported within one
# minor version of the API server, so 1.35 is the oldest accepted here.
# Arguments go after `--`: mise appends them to the command, so
# `mise run nexus-bench:up -- --namespace nexus-bench-2` reaches the command.
# Every flag has a NEXUS_BENCH_* variable; see `nexus-bench <subcommand> -h`.

[tasks."nexus-bench:up"]
description = "Deploy the disposable Nexus bench and its upstream on the cluster, wait for it, provision it, seed the data set and write the descriptor (acts on the cluster; --accept-eula needed once; seeding needs skopeo on this machine)"
tools = { kubectl = "1.35" }
run = "go run ./internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench up"

[tasks."nexus-bench:provision"]
description = "Provision the running Nexus bench again (idempotent) and write the descriptor (acts on the cluster)"
tools = { kubectl = "1.35" }
run = "go run ./internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench provision"

[tasks."nexus-bench:down"]
description = "Delete the Nexus bench namespace and wait until it is gone (acts on the cluster)"
tools = { kubectl = "1.35" }
run = "go run ./internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench down"

[tasks."nexus-bench:seed"]
description = "Put the data set in the Nexus bench that up provisioned and write the descriptor (acts on the cluster; needs skopeo on this machine, which mise does not install)"
tools = { kubectl = "1.35" }
run = "go run ./internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench seed"

[tasks."nexus-bench:cut-upstream"]
description = "Scale the Nexus bench upstream to zero replicas and wait until no pod is left (acts on the cluster; the proxy then serves only what it cached)"
tools = { kubectl = "1.35" }
run = "go run ./internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench cut-upstream"

[tasks."nexus-bench:restore-upstream"]
description = "Bring the Nexus bench upstream back and put its proxy back in service (acts on the cluster; needs skopeo on this machine, which mise does not install)"
tools = { kubectl = "1.35" }
run = "go run ./internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench restore-upstream"

[tasks."nexus-bench:reset"]
description = "Delete the Docker repositories and the upstream storage of the Nexus bench, then provision and seed again, keeping the instance (acts on the cluster; needs skopeo on this machine, which mise does not install)"
tools = { kubectl = "1.35" }
run = "go run ./internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench reset"

[tasks."nexus-bench:status"]
description = "Report on the Nexus bench: pod, REST answer, upstream, descriptor drift, data set (reads the cluster, changes nothing)"
tools = { kubectl = "1.35" }
run = "go run ./internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench status"

[tasks."nexus-bench:record"]
description = "Regenerate the recorded Nexus fixtures from the bench (needs the bench up and its data set as described)"
run = "go run ./internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench record"

[tasks."nexus-bench:render"]
description = "Print the Nexus bench manifests for the current parameters (contacts nothing)"
run = "go run ./internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench render"

[tasks."nexus-bench:test"]
description = "Run the integration tests against a running Nexus bench (acts on the cluster; skipped when CI is set)"
tools = { kubectl = "1.35" }
# env as a table, not `env DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH=1 go test`: the same line then
# works under bash and under the cmd shell mise uses on Windows.
env = { DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH = "1" }
# -timeout 60m: go test stops at 10 minutes by default and the lifecycle test
# (DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_LIFECYCLE=1) refuses to start with less than 45 left.
run = "go test -timeout 60m -count=1 -run Integration ./internal/nexusbench/..."

Usage: nexus-bench up [flags]

Check the cluster, deploy the bench and its upstream, wait for Nexus, provision it, put docker-proxy back in service when the upstream was cut, seed the data set and write the descriptor. Seeding needs skopeo on this machine (mise does not install it) unless NEXUS_BENCH_UPSTREAM_URL points at an upstream of your own.

A flag beats its NEXUS_BENCH_* variable, which beats the default.

Flags:
  -accept-eula
    	accept the Nexus Community Edition EULA on your behalf: read it first (default false; the variable counts only as the exact value yes)
  -anonymous
    	enable anonymous access, --anonymous=false to disable (default true)
  -context string
    	kubectl context of the cluster (default datomir)
  -cpu-limit string
    	CPU limit (default 2)
  -cpu-request string
    	CPU request (default 500m)
  -delete-timeout duration
    	how long down waits for the namespace to go (default 3m0s)
  -descriptor string
    	descriptor file (default internal/nexusbench/descriptor.json)
  -docker-nodeport int
    	NodePort of the Docker connector (default 30482)
  -hosts string
    	comma-separated hosts the NodePorts are tried on (default 127.0.0.1 and the node address)
  -http-nodeport int
    	NodePort of the REST API and the UI (default 30481)
  -image string
    	Nexus image, without the tag (default docker.io/sonatype/nexus3)
  -image-tag string
    	Nexus image tag (default 3.98.1)
  -jvm-opts string
    	JVM options of Nexus (default -Xms1g -Xmx1g -XX:MaxDirectMemorySize=1g -Djava.util.prefs.userRoot=/nexus-data/javaprefs)
  -memory-limit string
    	memory limit (default 4Gi)
  -memory-request string
    	memory request (default 3Gi)
  -namespace string
    	namespace of the bench, which down deletes (default nexus-bench)
  -rest-host string
    	host the REST API is reached on, and so the host the admin credentials are sent to (default 127.0.0.1); another host sends them in clear text. It concerns the REST API only: the images always go through 127.0.0.1
  -secrets string
    	secrets file, outside the repository (default under $XDG_STATE_HOME/devdesk/nexus-bench)
  -storage-size string
    	size of the data volume (default 5Gi)
  -timeout duration
    	how long up waits for Nexus, and how long the seed may run (default 10m0s)

    	image of the bench upstream registry, without the tag (default docker.io/library/registry)
  -upstream-image-tag string
    	tag of the bench upstream registry image (default 3.0.0)
  -upstream-url string
    	upstream of the proxy repository (default http://bench-upstream.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local:5000)
Usage: nexus-bench record [flags]

Regenerate the recorded Nexus fixtures from the bench: each fixture request is replayed through the loopback ports with the stored credentials, after the data set of the bench has been compared with the descriptor, and the redacted answers are written back only when every one passed. A fixture that declares flow: bearer or flow: redirects is followed as DevDesk would, inside the origins of the bench. Uses no kubectl, except with --state, which reads the upstream (read only) and refuses a bench that is not in that state. A HEAD that can cache an image in the proxy is sent only with --allow-cache-effects, and the bench then needs a reset. --dataset-as-admin compares the data set with the admin listing, for a bench whose anonymous access is cut. DEVDESK_FIXTURE_DENYLIST names a file of extra terms (one per line) no fixture may hold.

`<url>/<prefix>/<repo>:<tag>` — so they cannot mean two different repositories.
That disagreement is exactly what D39 was: `NexusDetector` synthesised a member
as `host/repository/<name>`, which browses (200) and cannot pull (404), because
the Docker client puts `/v2/` first and the whole path after it.

Like `provider`, it is **declared, never sniffed**. Whether a repository answers
on a path prefix, a connector port or a subdomain is a setting on that repository
(`docker.httpPort`, `docker.httpsPort`, `docker.subdomain`), and the one endpoint
carrying it answers 403 to an ordinary pull account — the same endpoint that
would say what a group's members are. An instance that refuses one refuses both,
so guessing is not a fallback, it is the defect.

The same declaration drives the image search header (DEVDESK-308, reworded by
DEVDESK-629): a `provider: nexus` + `kind: group` entry, its discovered members
and a declared entry with `parent: <slug>` pointing at such a group get a role
(group, proxy, hosted, from the member's `Type` that discovery stores), and the
browser's level 1 header says on a `May omit images` line which of them may not
have listed every image. The provider is read from the config
(`config.IsNexusGroup`), never guessed from the URL. See `network.md`, "Level 1
header summary".

The image search (`network.md`, `CatalogSearcher`, DEVDESK-306) reads the same
pair, with `auth_mode` through `credsFor`. Two ways to read a catalog:

- **A Nexus member** (a discovered member of a `provider: nexus` group, or a
  `parent:` entry of one, DEVDESK-579) is read on its own path,
  `/v2/<repo_prefix>/_catalog`. Nexus answers with names that do not carry the
  prefix; DevDesk rebuilds `<repo_prefix>/<name>`. An empty catalog is "no
  result"; a 404, 401, 403 or 405 is refused. One walk per member.
- **Any other entry** walks the root catalog of its host (`/v2/_catalog`), keeps
  the names under `<repo_prefix>/` and matches the typed text on the part after
  it. A catalog with no name under the prefix is refused, not "no result".
  Entries that share an API URL and an identity share one walk per search
  (DEVDESK-311, `network.md`); an entry with other credentials, another port or
  another subdomain is walked on its own.
  members, the cached ones stay, and the log says the redirect was refused. The
  anonymous retry of the members endpoint starts on any error except this
  refusal. Each Nexus reply is read up to 1 MiB (`maxNexusResponse`, not
  measured); a larger one is an error, not a silent cut. A format endpoint
  that answers 401, 403 or the Nexus 404 (below) is logged with the advice
  `account may lack nx-repository-admin privilege` and is a refusal (above);
  the origin refusal has its own log message, without that advice, and is a
  failed discovery. No members come back in either case.

4. docs/architecture/network.md, ligne Redirects du tableau « Measured Nexus behavior » : « contradicted » est trop fort, votre doute du tech-writer est fondé. La note NX-05 dit seulement : aucune redirection de même origine observée ; hors origine « non concluant » (blob store fichier, pas de S3, pas de reverse proxy, rien lu via proxy ou groupe). Écrire « none observed on this bench; off-origin: inconclusive ». Même dérive sur « Bearer flow completes: contradicted » : network.md les marque contredits, D169 ne les liste pas.

- network.md : la nouvelle section est insérée au milieu du bloc « Level 1 header summary ». « Each name list is fitted by fitNames… » se retrouve orphelin après elle ; la déplacer après ce bloc.
- D169 critère 2 : « no bench account was refused on _catalog » est imprécis (badcred 401 BASIC et la racine 404 sont `refused`, rejoués) ; il manque un refus de droits. IS-16 critère 2 exige le résultat noté dans registries.md, et D169 dit « not checked ».
- network.md : « six repository names » devrait dire 3 dépôts et 6 noms d'images. « File blob store », « about 20 s » et l'écriture du HEAD dans le cache sont « rapporté » dans les notes sans être signalés comme tels. Le blocage est temporaire (21 à 79 s) et ce n'est pas dit dans la ligne.
- Ligne docs-site « 403 (or 404…) » : factuellement fondée (banc : pull 404, anonyme 403 ; le 403 pull vient d'une instance d'entreprise non versionnée). Nommer « Nexus 3.98.1 » plutôt que « the Nexus version measured ».
- « D161 contredit » : le 403 du 2026-08-10 est une observation d'une autre instance, non contredite (« non tranché ») ; nuancer.
- nexus-bench-usage.md : `--rest-host` n'accepte qu'une adresse loopback pour `record` ; « loopback by default » pour les NodePorts alors que `-hosts` vaut 127.0.0.1 et l'adresse du nœud.
- « parade » (français) reste dans D169.

Critères 4 à 6 : le critère 4 est tenu a minima (une phrase renvoyant à la section mesurée, avec le banc distingué de l'instance d'entreprise, jamais mesurée). Le 5 est dit (rien n'est fermé). La page d'usage du banc existe (/home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/.worktrees/docs/devdesk-514-nexus-docs-alignment/docs/nexus-bench-usage.md).
